title: Ecclesiastes 5
paragraphs: ¹ Guard your steps when you go to the house of God. Draw near to listen rather than to offer the sacrifice of fools, who do not know that they are doing wrong. ² Do not be quick with your mouth; do not be hasty in your heart to utter anything before God. God is in heaven and you are on earth, so let your words be few. ³ A dream comes when there are many concerns, and a fool's voice through many words. ⁴ When you make a vow to God, do not delay in fulfilling it. He has no pleasure in fools — fulfill your vow. ⁵ It is better not to make a vow than to make one and not fulfill it.

⁶ Do not let your mouth lead you into sin. And do not protest to the messenger, "My vow was a mistake." Why should God be angry at what you say and destroy the work of your hands? ⁷ Much dreaming and many words are meaningless. Therefore fear God. ⁸ If you see the poor oppressed in a district, and justice and rights denied, do not be surprised at such things; for one official is watched by a higher one, and over them both are others higher still. ⁹ The profit of the land is taken by all; even the king profits from the fields. ¹⁰ Whoever loves money never has enough; whoever loves wealth is never satisfied with their income. This too is meaningless.

¹¹ As goods increase, so do those who consume them. And what benefit are they to the owners except to feast their eyes on them? ¹² The sleep of a laborer is sweet, whether they eat little or much, but the abundance of the wealthy keeps them awake. ¹³ I have seen a grievous evil under the sun: wealth hoarded to the harm of its owners. ¹⁴ Or wealth lost through some misfortune, so that when they have children there is nothing left for them. ¹⁵ Everyone comes naked from their mother's womb, and just as they came, so they depart. They take nothing from their labor to carry in their hands.

¹⁶ This too is a grievous evil: as everyone comes, so they depart. And what do they gain, since they toil for the wind? ¹⁷ All their days they eat in darkness, with great frustration, sickness, and resentment. ¹⁸ This is what I have observed to be good: it is fitting for a person to eat and drink and find satisfaction in all their toil under the sun during the few days of life God has given them — for this is their lot. ¹⁹ Moreover, when God gives someone wealth and possessions, and the ability to enjoy them, to accept their lot and be glad in their work — this is a gift of God. ²⁰ They seldom reflect on the days of their life, because God keeps them occupied with gladness of heart.
